ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-Efficient Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation with active learning
PROPOSAL: Our first experiment uses the XLNet teacher and the smaller DistilBERT student, applying a modified version of the forward selection algorithm from active learning to select the k samples that best represent the task-relevant information. The experiment is run on the publicly available IMDB sentiment analysis dataset and the subjects are the 10 classes representing positive and negative sentiment. 
CONTROLS: Our baseline will be the simple random sampling approach commonly used in few-shot learning, and we will ablate the forward selection algorithm to evaluate its effectiveness. To validate the relevance of task-aware distillation to our results, we will also train a teacher- student pair on the entire dataset and compare this with our results using k samples.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Active learning selection of samples should improve over simple random sampling and result in a student model that approximately 95% as accurate as the baseline trained on the full dataset; it may fail if the teacher doesn't capture the task-relevant information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Revising knowledge distillation with mutual information maximization for task-aware learning
PROPOSAL: Our second experiment builds on the previous one by revising the task-aware knowledge distillation objective to use mutual information maximization between the teacher's output and the student's intermediate activations. This will enable the student to learn a more direct mapping from input to output, improving its generalization on the task at hand. We will apply this approach to the task of linguistic acceptability (grammaticality) judgment using the natural language inference task of the SNLI dataset.
CONTROLS: Our baseline will again be the random sampling approach, and we will also train a teacher-student pair with the standard knowledge distillation loss for comparison. To ablate the mutual information maximization, we will run an experiment with just the standard knowledge distillation loss on the same dataset and student model.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This new approach should lead to an improved student model accuracy of around 92% on the task, compared to the 90% baseline with random sampling. However, it may struggle with the SNLI dataset's noisy labels, reducing its effectiveness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Characterizing few-shot performance with kernel regression analysis
PROPOSAL: Our third experiment takes a step back and tries to understand the intrinsic dynamics of few-shot learning with knowledge distillation. We propose to use kernel regression analysis to study the behavior of our task-aware knowledge distillation method from turns 1, particularly the choice of k samples for the teacher model's output. We will study the effect of using k samples of varying sizes on the student model's performance across several different tasks and input domains, including various product review datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare our kernel regression results with general knowledge distillation results on the same datasets and student models. Our ablation study will examine the contribution of the different components in the active learning process to the overall performance.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging kernel regression, we can identify specific sample Chairman members that contribute to the student model's performance and understand the decision boundaries of few-shot learning, but the choice of kernel might limit our findings to more universal prior distributions.

TITLE: Characterizing few-shot performance with kernel regression analysis
PROPOSAL: Revision: we modify the kernel regression analysis to include the teacher model's output and student model's output jointly, allowing us to better understand the interactions and dependencies between the two models. TITLE: Sample-Efficient Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation with active learning
PROPOSAL: Revision: we modify the active learning protocol to selectively sample the inputs that are most informative for the task, rather than just sampling the outputs. Specifically, we will use a mutual information-based approach to select the inputs that are most relevant to the task, and then use these inputs to distill the knowledge from the teacher model. This should help to reduce the effect of noise in the data and improve the efficiency of the few-shot learning protocol.
CONTROLS: Our controls remain the same as before, but we will add an additional ablation study to evaluate the contribution of the mutual information-based approach to the selection of informative inputs. 
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised active learning protocol should improve the efficiency of the few-shot learning protocol and reduce the effect of noise in the data, but it may require more careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Few-Shot Knowledge Distillation via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: Our new experiment proposes to use meta-learning to improve the efficiency of few-shot knowledge distillation. Specifically, we will frame the knowledge distillation process as a meta-learning problem, where the goal is to learn a meta-model that can adapt to new tasks and few-shot regimes. We will use a large dataset of tasks to train the meta-model, and then evaluate its performance on a set of novel tasks in few-shot regimes.
CONTROLS: Our baselines will include standard knowledge distillation and task-aware knowledge distillation without meta-learning. We will also ablate the meta-learning component to evaluate its contribution to the overall performance.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The meta-learning approach should improve the efficiency of few-shot knowledge distillation and enable the distillation of knowledge across multiple tasks. However, it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters and may struggle with tasks that have complex relationships between input and output.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 4
TITLE: Efficient Few-Shot Knowledge Distillation via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: Revision: we modify the meta-learning approach to include a hard example mining mechanism, which selectively samples the hardest examples from the training dataset to use during meta-training. This should help to improve the robustness and generalization of the meta-model to novel tasks and few-shot regimes. We will use a contrastive loss function to incentivize the meta-model to focus on the hardest examples.
CONTROLS: Our controls remain the same as before, but we will add an additional ablation study to evaluate the contribution of the hard example mining mechanism to the overall performance.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised meta-learning approach with hard example mining should further improve the efficiency and robustness of few-shot knowledge distillation, but it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters and may be sensitive to the choice of contrastive loss function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of Few-Shot Knowledge Distilled Models
PROPOSAL: Our new experiment evaluates the transferability of few-shot knowledge distilled models across different domains, tasks, and datasets. We will use a variety of transfer learning protocols to evaluate the performance of the distilled models on new tasks and domains, and compare the results to those obtained from training the models from scratch.
CONTROLS: Our baselines will include standard few-shot learning and task-aware knowledge distillation without transfer learning. We will also ablate the transfer learning protocol to evaluate its contribution to the overall performance.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The few-shot knowledge distilled models should exhibit good transferability across different domains, tasks, and datasets, but the extent of transferability will depend on the similarity between the training and testing environments.

TITLE: Towards a Theoretical Understanding of Few-Shot Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: Our final experiment takes a theoretical approach to understanding the success of few-shot knowledge distillation. We will derive a general probabilistic framework for few-shot knowledge distillation and provide a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties. This will help to identify the key factors that contribute to the efficacy of few-shot knowledge distillation and guide the design of more effective approaches.
CONTROLS: None required for this theoretical analysis.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (theoretical analysis only)
PREDICTION: Our theoretical framework should provide insights into the conditions under which few-shot knowledge distillation is successful and highlight the key challenges that need to be addressed in order to improve its performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Aware Distillation with Information-Theoretic Sample Selection
PROPOSAL: Develop a method that selects the k most informative samples from a labeled dataset for few-shot task-aware distillation of a large language model (LLM). This method uses information-theoretic metrics such as mutual information and conditional entropy to quantify the relevance of each sample to the task and the teacher model's decision-making process. The goal is to identify the most informative subset of samples that captures the teacher model's task behavior and decision-making, thereby improving the student model's performance in few-shot setting.
CONTROLS: Compare with random sampling, stratified sampling, and task-aware distillation without sample selection (i.e., using all k samples without selection).
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method will significantly outperform random and stratified sampling, and demonstrate competitive performance with task-aware distillation without sample selection. Expected to fail for tasks with highly correlated samples or when the teacher model is extremely powerful.

Assumes: Task-aware distillation framework is already established. Limited theoretical analysis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Generalizability of Task-Aware Distillation Methods
PROPOSAL: Investigate the generalizability of task-aware distillation methods on three real-world sentiment analysis tasks (movie reviews, product reviews, and restaurant reviews) and assess the degree to which they transfer knowledge across tasks. Specifically, fine-tune a pre-trained teacher model on each task and then use task-aware distillation to transfer knowledge to a smaller student model. Evaluate the student model's performance on the target task and on out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks that were not seen during training.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional teacher-student distillation and use ablation studies to evaluate the effect of task-specific fine-tuning and distillation.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Task-aware distillation methods will generalize well across tasks, with some degree of transfer learning observed. However, performance may degrade significantly on OOD tasks.

Assumes: Task-aware distillation framework is already established. Theoretical analysis on generalizability properties will be challenging. Focused on empirical evaluation.

ACTION: REVISION (1)
TITLE: Task-Aware Distillation with Information-Theoretic Sample Selection
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to incorporate a contrastive learning mechanism that encourages the student model to distinguish between relevant and irrelevant samples during the distillation process. This will help the student model to focus on the most informative samples for task learning and enhance its ability to generalize across different samples. Specifically, add a contrastive loss term to the distillation objective to push similar samples from the same class closer together and dissimilar samples from different classes further apart.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal and evaluate the impact of contrastive learning on few-shot task performance.
COST: No additional GPU-hours required, assuming the original 10 GPU-hours proposal remains intact.
PREDICTION: This revision will significantly improve the student model's ability to learn from informative samples and generalize across different samples, leading to better few-shot performance.

Assumes: The original proposal is feasible, and contrastive learning can be incorporated without altering the sample selection process excessively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Attack-Based Evaluation of Task-Aware Distillation
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial attack framework to evaluate the robustness of task-aware distillation methods against attacks designed to mislead the student model on specific task goals. This framework will use various adversarial attack methods (e.g., FGSM, PGD) to manipulate input samples in a way that makes the task-aware distillation impossible. The goal is to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed task-aware distillation framework under adversarial attacks and provide insights into its limitations.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional teacher-student distillation and evaluate the effect of different attack budgets and techniques on task-aware distillation performance.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Task-aware distillation methods will demonstrate resilience to minor adversarial attacks, but will fail to generalize when subjected to strong attacks that exploit the distilled knowledge. 

Assumes: Adversarial attacks are generated using gradient-based methods and that task-aware distillation mechanism could be robust under certain level of attacks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identifying Informative Examples for Few-Shot Task-Aware Distillation
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to annotate and categorize examples in a dataset based on their relevance to the few-shot task. This will involve labeling each example with a confidence score indicating its effectiveness as an informative example for the distillation process. The goal is to provide a subjective evaluation of the challenges associated with identifying informative examples in few-shot settings and develop a quantifiable metric to characterize the usefulness of individual samples.
CONTROLS: Compare with automatic methods for example ranking and evaluate the inter-annotator agreement among multiple human raters.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (manual annotation and annotation validation) + 10 GPU-hours (model evaluation)
PREDICTION: Human raters will show moderate to high agreement in assigning confidence scores, and the developed metric will reveal a subset of highly informative examples that can significantly improve the student model's performance.

Assumes: Manual annotation is feasible with a manageable inter-annotator agreement and the examples' informativeness can be characterized quantitatively through confidence scores.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Knowledge Transfer from Large-Scale Language Models to Sparse Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of transferring knowledge from a pre-trained large-scale language model (LLM) to a sparse neural network (SNN) using task-aware distillation. The goal is to explore the potential for sparse representations in reduced-size language models, which could alleviate computational burdens in resource-constrained environments. Evaluate the student model's performance on various benchmarks and compare with traditional pruning techniques.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional pruning and use ablation studies to evaluate the effect of sparse connections on task performance.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Task-aware distillation will facilitate the successful transfer of knowledge from the LLM to the SNN, but the resulting model may require additional optimization to achieve state-of-the-art performance.

Assumes: The task-aware distillation framework can accommodate sparse neural networks and that the transfer learning of sparse connections is feasible.

ACTION: REVISION (4)
TITLE: Identifying Informative Examples for Few-Shot Task-Aware Distillation
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to focus on domain adaptation rather than merely informative examples. Specifically, develop a method to actively adapt the teacher model's decision boundaries to the target task, thereby improving the student model's transferability and robustness in few-shot scenarios. This involves learning a representation Transform (RT) that adjusts the teacher's features to align with those from the target domain, while preserving the teacher's original decision boundaries.
CONTROLS: Compare with using the source domain's decision boundaries directly and evaluate the Domain adaptation Transfer metric.
COST: Additional 15 GPU-hours to learn the optimal Representation Transform (RT).
PREDICTION: By adapting the teacher model's decision boundaries to the target task using the RT, the student model will achieve better generalization and robustness in few-shot scenarios, at the cost of possible increased representational risk.

Assumes: The teacher model's decision boundaries are learnable and domain-agnostic, and the RT can be successfully learned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Teacher-Student Matching for Task-Aware Distillation
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to dynamically match the teacher model and student model at various stages of training, based on their shared knowledge and target task specifics. This adaptive matching involves sampling teacher-student pairs that are most informative for the target task, and repeating the process multiple times during training to adapt to task changes and student learning dynamics.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional fixed-teacher and fixed-student approaches, and evaluate the impact of different matching strategies on task performance.
COST: 25 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Adaptive teacher-student matching will significantly improve the student model's performance by dynamically adapting to the changing distributions of teacher and student knowledge, particularly on complex tasks that require knowledge transfer across multiple stages.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Task-Aware Distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of meta-learning for few-shot task-aware distillation, where the goal is to train a model that can learn quickly and adapt to new few-shot tasks with limited training data. Specifically, develop a meta-learning approach that learns to distill knowledge from pre-trained models to a fine-tuned model for unseen few-shot tasks, and evaluate its performance on other tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional few-shot learning approaches and evaluate the impact of meta-learning on task performance and adaptation capabilities.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Meta-learning will significantly improve the student model's adaptability and performance on unseen few-shot tasks, enabling the model to learn quickly and generalize better across diverse tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Framework for Task-Aware Distillation in Few-Shot Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive framework that integrates the various approaches and methods proposed in the previous studies, aiming to provide a unified solution for task-aware distillation in few-shot learning. The framework will incorporate information-theoretic sample selection, adaptive teacher-student matching, meta-learning, and knowledge transfer to achieve state-of-the-art performance in few-shot learning scenarios.
CONTROLS: Compare with the individual approaches and evaluate the performance of the unified framework across various tasks and datasets.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (highly parallelized implementation of the unified framework)
PREDICTION: The unified framework will significantly improve the student model's performance and adaptability in few-shot learning scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art results and setting a new benchmark for task-aware distillation.

Assumes: The individual approaches and methods can be effectively integrated into a unified framework without significant computational overhead.

title: multi-task learning for few-shot knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating multi-task learning into few-shot knowledge distillation to enable the student model to learn multiple related tasks simultaneously, leveraging task-demonstrated expertise in a more efficient manner. Our method will modify the knowledge distillation loss to accommodate multiple tasks, allowing the student model to learn from multiple teacher models representing different tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our multi-task learning approach to standard single-task knowledge distillation on a set of tasks, including sentiment analysis, sentiment intensity prediction, and aspect-based sentiment analysis.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our multi-task learning approach to improve knowledge distillation performance in few-shot learning scenarios by providing the student model with a more comprehensive understanding of the task space.

title: ensemble methods for few-shot knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: We propose using ensemble methods to combine the predictions of multiple student models, each trained with a different selection of examples, to improve the overall performance and robustness of the knowledge distillation process. Our ensemble method will adaptively select the best-performing student models and combine their predictions using a weighted average or bagging approach.
CONTROLS: We will compare our ensemble method to standard single-student knowledge distillation on various tasks and evaluation metrics.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our ensemble method to provide better or comparable performance to the state-of-the-art knowledge distillation methods while offering improved robustness to noisy or limited training data.

COST: 10 GPU-hours
